title: Tell a corner from an edge

blocks.text: A materials yard plans how many tonnes of each material to stock, under rules written as rows of $`Ax \le b`$. Its optimizer reports a plan, and the yard's analyst wants to check that the plan is a corner of the allowed region, as the optimum of a linear objective can always be chosen to be.

Write `is_extreme_point(A, b, x, tol=1e-9)` in `extreme.py`. `A` has one column per variable, so there are $`n`$ = `A.shape[1]` variables. Return `True` when `x` is an extreme point of $`\{x : Ax \le b\}`$:

items: `x` is feasible: every row has $`a_r^\top x \le b_r + \text{tol}`$;
among the **tight** rows, those with $`|a_r^\top x - b_r| \le \text{tol}`$, there are $`n`$ linearly independent ones. `np.linalg.matrix_rank(M)` returns how many independent rows `M` has.

blocks.text: Otherwise return `False`. Return a Python `bool`. The function must work for any number of variables, not only two.

# A tank farm: x0 litres of diesel and x1 of petrol (thousands).

A = np.array([[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1], [-1, 0], [0, -1]])
b = np.array([5, 4, 7, 0, 0])

for x in ([5, 2], [3, 4], [1, 1], [5, 1], [0, 0], [5, 4]):
    print(f"point {x}:", is_extreme_point(A, b, np.array(x)))

cases.says: a corner of the region is extreme and a point with no tight row is not
a feasible point with a single tight row is not extreme
a point where two rows cross but a third is broken is not extreme
a corner where more rows are tight than there are variables is still extreme
two tight rows that are multiples of each other do not make a corner
a corner whose coordinates are fractions is tight within the tolerance
in three variables a corner needs three independent tight rows

origin.section: Extreme Points Are Where Two Rows Are Tight at Once

concepts: a feasible point is a vertex when its tight rows include as many independent rows as there are variables
